lines.text: It is the soul of a nation — the great Spanish bull, black and unbreakable, charging without fear. Spain, La Roja, champions of Europe, who play this game like no one alive.
But down from the Alps swoops the Eagle — sharp-eyed, disciplined, and utterly without fear. Tonight, the bull meets the eagle.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode eighty-seven. Spain, versus Austria. A knockout. Win, or the dream dies right here.
Spain arrive as the reigning kings of Europe, a machine of movement and touch. Austria arrive as the Eagle — organised, relentless, the team no giant enjoys facing.
Spain — La Roja, the Bull. Beautiful, ruthless, and hunting another crown.

Alvaro Morata leads the line and wears the armband — a captain who lives for the big goal. Lamine Yamal is the teenage wizard who bends games to his will. And Pedri pulls every string with impossible calm.
Rodri sits and controls the whole night, the best in the world at what he does. And Nico Williams burns down the wing with fearless pace.
Austria — the Eagle. Sharp, physical, and afraid of no badge and no name.

David Alaba marshals the back and wears the armband — a big-game leader who has won it all. Marcel Sabitzer drives box to box with power. And Marko Arnautovic brings the menace and the swagger up top.
Konrad Laimer runs all night and presses like a storm. And Christoph Baumgartner arrives late to punish any lapse.
So here is the riddle. Does the Bull charge through and take the crown? Or does the Eagle strike from the sky and stun the champions?
And stay with me — because this one turns, late, on a captain's nerve.
Here is how we see it. Austria come out fearless, pressing high, and the champions are rattled early by the speed and the steel.
The Eagle strikes first. The whole stadium freezes.
And it lands. Marcel Sabitzer smashes it home from the edge of the box. Austria lead. The Eagle has drawn blood.
But this bull does not stop. Spain steady, the ball begins to sing, and the pressure builds and builds.
And Lamine Yamal, just a teenager, curls it into the top corner. One — one. The bull is charging now.
And then, late, the captain. Alvaro Morata rises and heads it home. Two — one, Spain. The Bull has the crown in sight.
Two — one. Austria were magnificent, and fearless, and so nearly there — but Spain's bull found a way, the way champions do.
Our prediction — Spain two, Austria one. Morata, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And Austria leave with their heads high — the Eagle that shook the champions, undone only in the dying minutes.
Spain march on. The Bull, reminding the world that the kings of Europe still charge like no one else.
So you tell me — the bull, or the eagle? Comment SPAIN for La Roja — comment AUSTRIA for the Eagle of the Alps.
On the dust of the arena he has reigned forever — black, proud, and unbroken, the raw heart of a footballing nation. Legend eighty-seven — the Spanish Bull, El Toro, the Soul of La Roja.
The players write the night. But the Bull carries one truth — greatness is not never being knocked. It is lowering your horns and charging straight back.
